To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the introduction of refrigeration technology increased trade in temperature sensitive commodities by 9-13 percentage points.

the introduction of refrigeration in shipping containers caused an increase of new trade in reefer products of 13% between the years 1968 and the mid 70s, and that the effect is concentrated among non-traditional, exotic, and high quality products.

the introduction of refrigeration containers increased the likelihood of new exports in temperature sensitive commodities by 10 percentage points, and that this effect was stronger for non-traditional commodities and for countries that were not already trading these products.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of technological change on the emergence of new trade and the growth of existing trade.
the impact of technological change on the pattern of trade.
the impact of the containerization of international trade routes on new trade in temperature-sensitive products.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
containerization has been a major driver of the growth of new trade and that this effect was particularly pronounced for the trade of temperature sensitive commodities.
the introduction of reefers has had a significant and positive impact on the likelihood of new exports and imports of temperature sensitive products in the 5-digit product classification.
the introduction of refrigeration technology has had a positive and significant impact on trade.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
technological change has been an important driver of new trade and that technological change has a strong impact on the composition of trade flows.
technological change in the transport industry has had a substantial effect on new trade and the composition of trade.
technological change in transportation technology has a strong impact on the emergence of new trade.
The main takeaway from our work is that
trade liberalization and technological change interact and can reinforce one another to generate new trade in temperature-sensitive products.
the introduction of a new technology that allows for a better preservation of temperature sensitive products can have a substantial impact on the likelihood of new products being traded.

the containerization has had an important impact on trade flows in temperature sensitive products, and that the introduction of refrigeration has been an important driver of the growth in trade in non-bulk, temperature sensitive products.
